candidates.zero_claim_prose_status: conditional; do not apply unless a reusable authoring Rule/Method owns and preserves the two fence invariants

clause_disposition.text: Use prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express.
clause_disposition.kind: authoring Method guidance, not a Property invariant
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Remove from this Property Claim and retain in a shared authoring Method or general Claim rule. The currently inspected Declaration Form registration Rule limits this guidance to Declaration content and is not sufficient for all RMED Roles.

clause_disposition.text: At most one CFEL block is present.
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Preserve in this Claim until a shared Rule/Method explicitly owns it. Current CFEL has no Markdown fence-count operator.

clause_disposition.text: Other fenced blocks are not allowed in Claim.
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Preserve in this Claim until a shared Rule/Method explicitly owns it. Current CFEL has no Markdown fence-label exclusion operator.

candidates.why_no_new_syntax: Fence counting has only this inspected consumer. The user requires reusable syntax for at least two consumers and prohibits an opaque single-use predicate. Route the serialization rule to shared authoring authority instead of inventing a Claim-specific operator.

supporting_pins.finding: A CFEL-labelled fenced block carries formal content inside Claim, but this does not constrain the number of blocks or disallow other fence labels.
Requires CFEL for expressible constraints and prose for remaining ones in Declaration content; not a general RMED Claim rule.

candidates.subject: Atom.Subjects.Passive
candidates.zero_claim_prose_status: not supported by existing CFEL; do not remove the direct-context or distinctness invariant

clause_disposition.text: Passive Subjects identify distinct direct contextual dependencies.
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Retain in the Claim or transfer intact to a shared governing Rule before removing it. The value/count clauses below only declare a list of strings and do not encode what they refer to or whether values repeat.

candidates.why_no_new_syntax: Existing UNIQUE is cross-instance tuple uniqueness, not distinct values within one Property. A new intra-Property distinctness assertion would have only one identified consumer and would not by itself establish direct contextual-reference validity. Do not invent a parser predicate or weaken the direct dependency requirement.

supporting_pins.source: Draft separation of Property values and child constraints
supporting_pins.finding: Property value cardinality and dependent-name constraints are separate; it does not define intra-list value uniqueness.
UNIQUE compares Property tuples across selected logical instances, not repeated scalar values on one bearer.

candidates.subject: Atom.Tier
candidates.zero_claim_prose_status: not safe until equivalent owner/purpose constraints are carried by target-model authority

clause_disposition.text: Project Goals use Tier -1 and Operator ownership.
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Preserve the constraint. CFEL has numeric comparisons and Role/Form qualification, but the selected packet does not provide a settled Project Goal Form admission or a general Atom-to-Operator ownership binding. The inspected HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT Relation Draft is restricted to Requirement Declaration→Node, so it cannot establish Project Goal Operator ownership.

clause_disposition.text: Ordinary Scope Unit-owned Atoms use Tier 0 or higher.
clause_disposition.candidate_action: Preserve the constraint. The selected packet does not define a safe owner-kind binding that distinguishes Scope Unit ownership from the Project Goal Operator exception. Do not infer owner from storage, containment, or a Target Scope Unit.

candidates.why_no_new_syntax: The formal integer domain, optional Label child and general lower bound are already expressible. The remaining clauses require owner/purpose classification and identity links, which are not declared for these cases. A single-purpose predicate would hide unresolved relations; use a reusable target-model Rule or settle those bindings first.

supporting_pins.source: Current CA-R-2132 Project Goal Tier and owner Rule
supporting_pins.finding: Project Goal is currently identified by Requirement Type Project Goal and requires Operator ownership plus Tier -1. This is legacy source evidence, not a replacement target-model declaration.

supporting_pins.source: Current CA-R-2125 and CA-R-2131 ordinary owner Tier Rules
supporting_pins.finding: Ordinary/non-Project Goal Atoms owned by Scope Units use integer Tier >=0. These Current Rules are evidence for preservation, not sufficient replacement authority if the migration retires them.
Its endpoint declaration is limited to Requirement Declaration Atoms linking to the Node branch; it is not a general Atom-to-Operator / Atom-to-Scope-Unit ownership relation.

shared_or_method_disposition.claim_authoring_guidance: Move 'Use prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express' to a reusable authoring Method or general Rule; current Declaration-form rule is narrower.
shared_or_method_disposition.claim_fence_invariants: Keep the one-CFEL-fence/no-other-fence requirements in this Claim until a shared authoring Rule/Method owns them. No one-off CFEL operator is proposed.
shared_or_method_disposition.passive_dependency_invariant: Keep direct contextual dependency and within-list distinctness in the Claim or a shared Rule. Current CFEL cannot express them safely.
shared_or_method_disposition.tier_owner_invariants: Keep both owner-scoped Tier clauses in the Claim until the target-model Rule expresses Project Goal identity, Operator ownership, and Scope Unit ownership. The `>= -1` CFEL line does not replace them.

unresolved_real_decisions: Which shared authoring Rule/Method will own prose-vs-CFEL guidance and Claim fence constraints across RMED Roles? Until then, removing the fence clauses would weaken the invariant.

Which target-model declaration establishes Project Goal Form identity and general Atom-to-Operator / Atom-to-Scope-Unit ownership so the two Tier clauses can be formalized or transferred without relying on retiring Current Rules?

No new CFEL syntax is recommended in this lane: the missing pieces are content serialization, passive-reference semantics, and ownership bindings; the identified candidate operators would each be one-off or opaque.
